scripts.radio:
Good evening, you are listening to Kenya on Record. In Tana River County, tragedy has struck again as over three hundred families find themselves displaced by severe flooding. Homes have been submerged, farms washed away, and hundreds of men, women, and children are in desperate need of emergency shelter, clean drinking water, and food supplies.

While our immediate appeal goes to the Red Cross and emergency response teams to secure these families, we must confront the uncomfortable truth of governance. Tana River does not flood by surprise. The seasonal patterns are known, early warnings are issued, and public budgets regularly allocate millions toward disaster preparedness and climate adaptation. Yet year after year, the response remains reactive—waiting for villages to sink before dispatching temporary tents and a few bags of maize.

Where are the permanent dykes? What happened to the promised structured resettlement programs out of the flood plains? Our people cannot remain perpetual victims of poor planning while disaster response funds disappear into bureaucratic pockets. Relief must reach Tana River today, but long-term accountability must follow tomorrow.

Kwa ufupi, zaidi ya familia mia tatu katika kaunti ya Tana River zimekosa makao kufuatia mafuriko makali. Wanahitaji hifadhi na chakula cha dharura mara moja. Hata hivyo, viongozi wa kaunti na serikali ya kitaifa lazima wawajibike: mbona hakuna mikakati ya kudumu kuzuia janga hili linalojirudia kila mwaka? Tusikubali uzembe huu uendelee.
scripts.voice_note: Habari zenu, this is Kenya on Record with an urgent update. In Tana River, over three hundred families are out in the cold after severe floods swept through their villages. They need emergency shelter, clean water, and food assistance immediately. But as we push for rapid relief, we have to demand accountability. Flooding in the lower Tana basin is not a sudden accident—it is a regular, seasonal occurrence. Every financial year, funds are set aside for disaster mitigation and water management, yet our people are still abandoned to rely on emergency handouts when the rains peak. Support must reach the ground right now, but county and national leaders must tell us why long-term flood control projects are never completed. Let's stay vigilant and hold them to account.
scripts.sms: Usiibiwe: When donating to flood relief, send aid only through verified local leaders or registered Red Cross channels to avoid rogue fundraisers cashing in.
scripts.reels: Over three hundred families in Tana River are homeless tonight following severe floods. They urgently need shelter and food, but here is the real issue: this crisis happens every single year. Why are we still doing emergency handouts instead of permanent flood mitigation? Disaster budgets must serve the people, not enrich contractors. Immediate relief now, full accountability next.
